subject.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy

question: Should Codex heartbeat, cron, and inter-session turns carrying the internal WebChat marker be treated as unbound and therefore allowed to send across providers under the default cross-context policy?
rationale: The patch deliberately restores autonomous delivery by changing which turns participate in a cross-provider containment boundary; source and proof support the narrow implementation, but automation cannot establish the intended authority of every inter-session turn or approve that policy exception.

options.title: Approve the narrow internal-turn exception
options.body: Confirm these three turn classes are trusted internal execution, refresh against current main, and merge while keeping genuine WebChat and real-channel turns bound.

options.title: Keep fail-closed routing
options.body: Require an explicit cross-context configuration allowance for autonomous sends and separately surface policy denials through heartbeat or handoff results.

options.title: Pause for a broader boundary design
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and pause this PR if inter-session provenance cannot reliably distinguish trusted internal work from user-derived authority.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow internal-turn exception
recommendation.body: Confirm these three turn classes are trusted internal execution, refresh against current main, and merge while keeping genuine WebChat and real-channel turns bound.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the recent merged work on Codex internal-turn dynamic-tool behavior in the same modules.
